# Nvidia—Wall Street Is Missing China-Linked Margin Risk—Buybacks Support Stock

![](https://thearorareport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/NVDA-Chart-2026-11-18_08h16_07.jpg)

#### **Wall Street Misses NVDA’s Margin Risk**

Please click [here](https://thearorareport.com/stock-market-chart-analysis-nvidia-margins-earnings-china-money-flows-mc-18) for an enlarged chart of **NVIDIA Corp** [(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA).

Note the following:

- This article is about the big picture, not an individual stock. The chart of NVDA stock is being used to illustrate the point. Nvidia earnings, along with **Anthropic’s** (ANT) IPO, President Trump’s visit to Asia, FOMC minutes, positioning, money flows, sentiment, and technicals, are the most important elements driving the stock market at this time.
- The chart shows that NVDA stock has risen after earnings.
- The chart shows that in spite of very strong earnings and guidance, the [bulls’ hopium](https://www.benzinga.com/opinion/26/11/63352031/nvidia-earnings-first-without-huang-options-market-signals-8-5-stock-move) did not come true.
- The chart shows that the bears’ hopium also did not come true.
- It is worth a reminder that hopium is not a good investment strategy.
- In our analysis, based on earnings and guidance alone, NVDA stock should have been up 15% – 20% this morning.
- Wall Street is almost unanimously very bullish after earnings.
- In our analysis, the reason for the subdued stock market reaction is the unanswered questions.
- **In our analysis, NVDA appears to be putting a floor under NVDA stock by stepping up buybacks.** NVDA bought back \$22.1 billion of stock last quarter and plans to spend another \$227.3 billion by the end of fiscal 2028. This works out to about \$45 billion per quarter over the next five quarters, more than double the latest quarter. Such large buybacks could help support NVDA stock.
- In yesterday’s Morning Capsule, we gave you eight questions to focus on during NVDA’s earnings and conference call. Here are the answers.
  - Will NVDA beat expectations? Yes. Revenue was \$115.8 billion versus \$109 billion expected. Adjusted EPS was \$2.68 versus \$2.48 expected. Whisper numbers were higher than consensus. NVDA beat the whisper numbers.
  - How will NVDA guidance measure up to expectations? NVDA guided to \$130 billion in fourth quarter revenue versus about \$125 billion expected. Fiscal 2028 revenue growth guidance was raised from 70% to 75%.
  - **How much NVDA revenue is at risk from China? Our most important question went unanswered. NVDA disclosed \$2.4 billion in Hopper chip sales to China. NVDA interim CEO Colette Kress said that China revenue was about 10%. However, in our analysis, this is misleading, as a significant portion of the revenue comes indirectly from China through customers in other countries. We previously estimated that direct and indirect China revenue is in the range of 12% – 20% of NVDA sales.**
  - Can NVDA maintain its extraordinary gross margins? Gross margins were 74.9%. NVDA expects 71% – 72% next quarter and 72% – 73% in fiscal 2028. Both are below the latest reported level.
  - Is the Vera Rubin rollout on track? Yes. NVDA reported nearly \$20 billion in first quarter production shipments, its fastest ramp ever.
  - Are hyperscalers still spending aggressively on AI? Yes. Hyperscaler revenue rose 23% to \$60.1 billion. Demand still exceeds supply.
  - How much of NVDA’s growth depends on financing customers and investing in companies that buy its chips? NVDA disclosed \$118 billion in maximum guarantee exposure and \$32 billion in future neocloud commitments. **What we still do not know is how much revenue depends on NVDA’s financial support of its customers.**
  - What will management say about finding a permanent CEO? The board is considering internal and external candidates and does not plan to bring Jensen Huang back. **We still do not know if NVDA can maintain its technology lead without Huang.**
- **Our second most important question was about gross margins. After earnings, Wall Street does not appear to be concerned. In our analysis, Wall Street may be missing the gross margin risk.** Here are the key points:
  - Wall Street was pleased with NVDA’s earnings and guidance. However, analysts did not ask how losing China linked customers could affect future gross margins.
  - The Trump administration is tightening restrictions on Chinese companies accessing American AI computing through data centers in other countries. NVDA has also formed a new board committee to oversee export controls.
  - Yesterday, we shared our analysis that direct and indirect China related sales may account for 12% – 20% of NVDA revenue. NVDA did not disclose enough to determine how close our estimate is to the actual number.
  - There are plenty of buyers for NVDA chips. Even if NVDA loses China-linked customers, it may be able to sell those chips elsewhere without much impact on revenue.
  - **Here is what Wall Street may be missing. Losing China-linked customers could leave NVDA more dependent on a few very large hyperscalers. These customers may gain bargaining power and negotiate lower prices, hurting gross margins.**
  - NVDA is guiding to 72% – 73% gross margins for fiscal 2028. This guidance was first issued before the latest China restrictions and was reaffirmed yesterday. It remains to be seen whether NVDA can meet this guidance if it loses more China-linked business.
- **In our analysis, NVDA may be able to replace China-linked sales, but not necessarily at the same gross margins. The risk may become more significant in fiscal 2029 as large customers gain bargaining power and alternatives to NVDA chips improve.**
- For the very short term, continue to watch smart money flows and momo crowd money flows. Strong earnings do not settle the bigger questions about China, gross margins, and NVDA’s future without Jensen Huang.
  - In the early trade, momo crowd money flows are very positive in NVDA.
  - In the early trade, smart money flows are very positive in NVDA.
- As a full disclosure, on our long core NVDA position from \$12.55, partial profits have been taken.
- Demand for Anthropic (ANT) appears to be strong. The IPO will be priced tonight, and ANT will start trading tomorrow.
- President Trump has arrived in China for the APEC summit. President Xi personally welcomed him at the airport. Trump is expected to meet with Xi and Russian President Putin on Thursday, with trade, Ukraine, and nuclear weapons among the topics.
- **In our analysis, a big issue for investors is whether Trump and Xi can make progress on AI chips and trade, especially with China threatening to retaliate against the latest U.S. export restrictions.**

 

- FOMC minutes will be released at 2 pm ET and may be market moving.
